facts.F1: Follow-up from fix-review-app-repos-link (docs/feature/fix-review-app-repos-link/rca.md:16-24): scan.rs discards mark_repo_read (scan.rs:669) and record_account_checks (scan.rs:380) errors with let _ =, so a failed store write leaves a completed run showing '0 repos read'; and the queue shows repos_read_message for any completed run (views/queue.rs:651-653), including runs stored before scan plans existed, where '0 repos read' is misleading. User decisions 2026-11-08: when a store write fails during a scan, end the run Interrupted (as an unreadable source list does, scan.rs:663), so the queue offers Resume scan and resume re-reads repos not yet marked read; for a completed run with no plan rows, hide the repos-read line.
facts.F10: A signed-in owner whose latest completed run has no scan_run_repos rows opens the queue; and, as a control, one whose latest completed run has plan rows.
facts.F11: The first queue has no 'repos read' status line; the control queue shows 'N repos read' with its true count, including '0 repos read' when every planned repo is unread.
facts.F12: The legacy run's queue shows '0 repos read', or a planned run's count line disappears.
facts.F13: When a scan cannot write its results to the store, the run ends in the Interrupted state and never reports itself as Completed.
facts.F14: An interrupted scan can be run again and resumes that run, instead of forcing the user to abandon it and start over.
facts.F15: A run whose store write failed never shows a repos-read count that claims more repos were read than the store actually holds for that run.
facts.F16: A completed run that had no planned repos shows no repos-read line at all, rather than a zero or placeholder count.
facts.F17: A completed run that had planned repos still shows its repos-read line, with the true number of repos read for that run.
facts.F18: A signed-in owner starts a scan on a development build started with the review app's test-fault seam naming a refused scan write: refuse_mark_repo_read (the store refuses marking a planned repo read) or, separately, refuse_record_account_checks (the store refuses recording the run's account checks). The owner then restarts without the fault and resumes.
facts.F19: A signed-in owner whose latest completed run was kept by the release before this app stored a scan plan opens her queue.
facts.F2: The review app's 'repos read' line is true: a scan whose store writes fail ends Interrupted and can be resumed, and a run stored before scan plans existed shows no repos-read line.
facts.F20: Her queue is a finished scan's queue, shows exactly the suggestions that were kept, and says nothing at all about repos read.
facts.F21: She is no longer told her scan read none of her repos when nothing about which repos it read was ever recorded.
facts.F22: The line is hidden for every run whose count is nought, plan or no plan; the planned-run-that-read-nothing case rejects that.
facts.F23: A signed-in owner who saved a choice of five repos, and whose latest scan read exactly those five, opens her queue.
facts.F24: Her queue says five repos read, the true count of the repos that scan read.
facts.F25: She still sees how many of her repos her scan read.
facts.F26: The count reports planned repos rather than repos read, which agrees here because all five planned repos were read; the planned-run-that-read-nothing case rejects that.
facts.F27: A signed-in owner who chose one repo that was archived after her choice, and whose scan then finished having read no repo, opens her queue.
facts.F28: Her queue names that repo as the one it could not read and says nought repos read.
facts.F29: She can tell a scan that read none of her chosen repos from a run that never recorded any, because the first still reports its count.
facts.F3: A scan whose store write fails ends Interrupted and is resumable, never Completed with a wrong repos-read count.
facts.F30: The line is kept for every completed run, plan or no plan; the run kept from before scan plans were stored rejects that.
facts.F4: A scan whose store write fails (marking a repo read, or recording an account's check) ends Interrupted, and the queue offers Resume scan instead of a completed '0 repos read'.
facts.F43: A signed-in owner whose review store refuses to save how her GitHub accounts' checks ended starts a scan; then the store accepts those writes again and she picks the unfinished scan up from her queue.
facts.F44: The scan ends interrupted, her queue offers only to resume it and claims no repos read at all; resuming reads her repos, finishes, and her queue then accounts for exactly as many repos as the resumed scan read, no more and no fewer.
facts.F45: A scan whose record of her account checks could not be saved is shown to her as interrupted and resumable, not as a finished scan that read no repos, and the count she finally sees is the true one.
facts.F46: The run ends interrupted before any repo is read, so the check that no repo whose read was never saved is skipped has nothing to compare; a scan that instead read some repos and then ended interrupted would also pass. It still loses nothing, because the resume reads the repos again and the queue then accounts for exactly those, so this promise is not broken.
facts.F47: The probe admits two commands: openlore-review-app and review-app-oracle. "openlore-review-app serve --help" lists no options at all ("Usage: openlore-review-app serve"), so no fault seam, fixture sign-in or queue route is reachable by starting the server directly; the declared review-app-oracle suites are therefore the designated public surface for these scenarios. At HEAD ad7687c those suites do render what the owner sees: each scenario prints a block headed "what she sees", the stored run status, the queue status region verbatim line by line, whether the repos-read line is PRESENT or ABSENT, whether "Resume scan" is offered, and the scan actions offered.
facts.F48: Probe "review-app-oracle store-failure --nocapture" (4 passed, 0 failed) printed the owner-visible result of both refused scan writes. For the store refusing to save that a repo was read, and separately for the store refusing to save her account checks, the first block reads identically on the points that matter: "the status her latest run is stored with: interrupted"; status region verbatim "| Your last scan was interrupted. The suggestions found so far are kept; press Resume scan to finish it."; "the repos-read line: ABSENT, her queue saying neither \"repos read\" nor \"repo read\" anywhere"; "\"Resume scan\": OFFERED"; "the scan actions her queue offers: Resume scan". No block reports the status completed for a run whose write was refused, and no repos-read count appears on either interrupted queue.
facts.F49: The same store-failure probe printed a second block per scenario, headed "the run she picked up over, her store saving again": "the status her latest run is stored with: completed", status region "| Ownership re-checked: priyaraman * - 5 new suggestions" then "| 3 repos read" for the refused account-checks scenario and "| Ownership re-checked: priyaraman * - 1 new suggestion" then "| 3 repos read" for the refused repo-read scenario, with "the repos-read line: PRESENT, reading \"3 repos read\"", "\"Resume scan\": not offered" and "the scan actions her queue offers: Scan again". So after the fault the owner resumes the run she had, and that picked-up run reaches completed with a repos-read count, rather than her having to abandon it and start over.
facts.F50: Limits of these captures. The suites print the rendered queue and the stored run status, but never a run identifier, so the resumed run is attested by the heading "the run she picked up" rather than by a printed id; they never list which individual repos the resumed scan read, so the S1 falsifier "resume skips a repo whose read was never stored" is not directly exercised by any printed per-repo set; and the count line is compared against the scenario heading ("the five repos she chose", "none of the one repo she chose") rather than against a separately printed store count. All evidence comes from the declared acceptance suites rendering the queue, not from a live signed-in session on an installed host.
facts.F51: A harness negative control fires in both suites at HEAD ad7687c: review_app::state_delta::tests::assert_state_delta_fails_on_hidden_mutation panics with: state-delta assertion failed: slot "hidden.slot": implicit-unchanged violated; before="original" after="mutated", reported as "should panic ... ok". The state-delta machinery detects an unexpected state change, which supports trusting the suites PRESENT/ABSENT reports, though it exercises the harness rather than the product.
facts.F52: Probe "review-app-oracle legacy-run --nocapture" (5 passed, 0 failed) printed three owner-visible queues. (a) The run kept before scan plans were stored: "the status her latest run is stored with: completed", status region exactly one line "| Ownership re-checked * - 10 new suggestions", and "the repos-read line: ABSENT, her queue saying neither \"repos read\" nor \"repo read\" anywhere". (b) Her scan having read none of the one repo she chose: completed, status region includes "| 0 repos read", "the repos-read line: PRESENT, reading \"0 repos read\"". (c) Her scan having read the five repos she chose: completed, status region includes "| 5 repos read", "the repos-read line: PRESENT, reading \"5 repos read\"". So the no-plan-rows run shows no line and no placeholder, while planned runs keep a count line whose number matches the repos the scenario had read.
facts.F53: A signed-in owner whose review store refuses to save that a repo was read starts a scan; her store then refuses to save how her GitHub accounts' checks ended instead, and she picks that unfinished run up from her queue; then the store accepts those writes again and she picks the run up once more.
facts.F54: Both the scan and the run she picked up under the still-refusing store end interrupted, and after each her queue offers only to pick that run up and claims no repos read at all; once the store accepts those writes, picking the run up reads every repo whose read was never saved, finishes, and her queue then accounts for exactly as many repos as that run read, no more and no fewer.
facts.F55: She is never told a scan finished when a save of it was refused - neither on her first scan nor when she picks the run up while her store is still refusing a write; she keeps picking that same run up rather than starting over, and the repos-read count she finally sees is one she can trust.
facts.F56: The run she picks up reads some of her repos before it meets the refused save and only then ends interrupted, provided it saves none of those reads. She loses nothing by that - the pick-up after the store recovers reads them again and the count she finally sees is still exactly the repos that run read - so this promise is not broken.
facts.F6: The run's stored status is Interrupted, the queue offers 'Resume scan', and no completed-run 'repos read' line is shown; resuming once the store accepts writes reads the repos not yet marked read.
facts.F7: The run ends Completed (or the queue shows a repos-read count) after a refused store write, or resume skips a repo whose read was never stored.
facts.F8: A completed run with no plan rows shows no repos-read line; a planned run keeps its true count.
facts.F9: A completed run stored before scan plans existed (no plan rows) shows no repos-read line on the queue; a run with plan rows still shows its count.
